13 Two spheres travel along the same line with velocities u1 and u2. They collide and after collision
their velocities are v1 and v2.
before collision u1
before collision u2
after collision v1
after collision v2
Which collision is not elastic?
u1 / m s–1
u2 / m s–1
v1 / m s–1
v2 / m s–1
A
2
–5
–5
–2
B
3
–3
0
6
C
3
–2
1
6
D
5
2
3
6

hints: Notice the signs of $u_1$, $u_2$, $v_1$ and $v_2$ in the table - negative means motion to the left along the same line.
Recall that for an elastic collision in one dimension the relative speed of approach equals the relative speed of separation: $u_1 - u_2 = v_2 - v_1$.
Calculate $u_1-u_2$ and $v_2-v_1$ for each row and look for the row where the two magnitudes are different.
walkthrough: Identify the test for a one-dimensional elastic collision: magnitude of relative velocity is conserved, so speed of approach equals speed of separation.
Write approach speed as $u_1 - u_2$ and separation speed as $v_2 - v_1$, keeping the signs from the table with units $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Check row A: approach $= 2 - (-5) = 7 \text{m s}^{-1}$ while separation $= -2 - (-5) = 3 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Check the other rows: B gives $6 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $6 \text{m s}^{-1}$, C gives $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$, D gives $3 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $3 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Only row A has different approach and separation speeds, so kinetic energy and relative speed are not conserved. This is option A

A.explanation: Speed of approach $7 \text{m s}^{-1}$ does not equal speed of separation $3 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so relative speed is not conserved and the collision is not elastic.

B.explanation: Speed of approach $3-(-3)=6 \text{m s}^{-1}$ equals speed of separation $6-0=6 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so this is elastic.

C.explanation: Speed of approach $3-(-2)=5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ equals speed of separation $6-1=5 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so this is elastic.

D.explanation: Speed of approach $5-2=3 \text{m s}^{-1}$ equals speed of separation $6-3=3 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so this is elastic.
